_comment: Firestore composite indexes for the AgentOS backend.
Until now every composite index in production was created BY HAND, from the
one-click link Firestore prints the first time a query fails. Nothing in the
repo recorded which indexes the code depends on, so a fresh project (or a
restored database) came up subtly broken and nobody could tell which query
needed what. This file is that record.
STATUS: the three 'required today' composites below (creative_events,
creatives, runs) WERE applied to the production database lsbrandkit on
2026-09-01 via the Firestore REST API and reached READY the same day. The
two mr_runs entries remain unapplied on purpose (not required yet).
Applying a new index stays a deliberate, separate step:
firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes --project <project>
or, per index, `gcloud firestore indexes composite create ...` against the
named database (the backend does NOT use '(default)' everywhere - see
settings.firestore_database).
Single-field equality filters are served by Firestore's automatic
single-field indexes and need NO entry here. That covers every query the
MR read-path work added: mr_runs filtered by (user_id) and by
(user_id, kind) - two equality filters with no ordering - and mr_snapshots
filtered by (vendor_slug) and (month). They were written that way on
purpose, so the cost fix could ship without waiting on an index build.
The first three entries below are the composites the code ALREADY requires today.

indexes._why: firestore_repo.list_usage_events - the per-user Home dashboard: where(user_id ==) + where(created_at >=). The inequality forces a composite.
firestore_repo.delete_ingested_creatives - where(brand_id ==) + where(creative_metadata.author ==). Two equality filters, one of them a nested field path.

firestore_repo.list_runs_for_user - the console's Runs panel and every figure Home derives from it: where(user_id ==) + order_by(created_at DESC) + limit. REQUIRED TODAY. Without it Firestore refuses the query and the code falls back to an unordered read sorted in process, which is correct but caps at 3000 rows per caller and costs a wasted round-trip on the first read of each 10-minute window.

NOT REQUIRED TODAY - the follow-up. mr_runs currently sorts in Python because the disk copies merge in after the query. The day that ordering + a limit move server-side (where(user_id ==) + order_by(generated_at DESC) + limit), this is the index it needs. Listed so it can be built BEFORE that change ships, not discovered by an outage after.
NOT REQUIRED TODAY - same follow-up, for the kind-scoped reads (/mr/datasets, /mr/runs, _load_dataset).
